title: Heat and temperature
examples: What is the difference between conduction and convection?
How does the Earth get heat from the Sun?
Can you explain how insulators work in a house?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how heat moves around us. We will look at three main ways heat moves.
Conduction is when heat moves through direct contact between materials. Think about touching a hot metal spoon. The heat moves up the spoon handle.
Convection happens when heat heats up a fluid like water or air. Hotter, less dense fluids rise up, and cooler, denser fluids sink down. This creates currents.
Radiation is heat that travels in waves, like invisible waves. The Sun heats the Earth using radiation. You feel this heat even without touching anything.
Insulators are materials that slow down the transfer of heat. Examples include wool or thick plastic. They keep heat either in or out.
In everyday life, think about a cup of hot chocolate. The mug itself is often made of ceramic, which is a good insulator. This keeps the heat inside the drink longer.

draw.text: Real Life: Ceramic mug keeps heat in

faq.q: Why does metal feel cold when it is actually room temperature?
faq.a: Metals are good conductors of heat. They transfer heat away from your hand very quickly, making them feel colder than they really are.
asks: Is it the temperature or the material?
Why does touching metal feel different?

faq.q: Is convection only about liquids, or can it happen with air too?
faq.a: Convection happens with any fluid, including air. This is how wind moves heat across the ground.
asks: Does air move heat by convection?

faq.q: Does radiation need anything to travel through, like air or vacuum?
faq.a: No, radiation can travel through a vacuum, like space. This is how the Sun's heat reaches Earth.
asks: How does the Sun heat us without air?

faq.q: Are all materials insulators? What about metals?
faq.a: No, most metals are good conductors, not insulators. Insulators are materials that resist the flow of heat.
asks: What is the opposite of an insulator?
Can a metal be an insulator?

faq.q: If I put a pot on a stove, which method of heat transfer is happening first?
faq.a: First, the heat from the flame transfers to the bottom of the pot by conduction. Then, the water inside will heat up by convection.
asks: What happens first when boiling water?
Do I see conduction or convection first?
Which method starts when heating water?

facts: Conduction requires direct physical contact between objects.
Convection currents move heat through liquids and gases.
Radiation transfers heat energy via electromagnetic waves.
Insulators slow down the rate of heat transfer.

quiz.say: Heat moving through the air when a room heats up is best described as:
quiz.why: Convection involves the movement of fluids, like air, which is what happens when a room heats up.

wrong.1: Conduction only happens when things touch directly, not when air moves.
wrong.2: Radiation travels as waves and does not require air movement to happen.
wrong.3: Insulation is a material property, not a method of heat transfer.

quiz.say: Which method of heat transfer allows the Sun's energy to reach Earth?
quiz.why: The Sun sends energy as waves through space, which is the definition of radiation.

wrong.0: Insulation describes slowing heat; it is not a transfer method itself.
wrong.2: Conduction requires physical contact, which is impossible across space.
wrong.3: Convection needs a fluid medium, and space is mostly a vacuum.

quiz.say: If you wrap a container of hot water in thick foam, you are mainly using which principle?
quiz.why: Foam is an insulator; its job is to slow down the rate at which heat escapes from the water.

wrong.0: The foam does not stop the movement of the water itself.
wrong.1: The foam is designed to stop all forms of heat loss, not just wave radiation.
wrong.3: While heat escapes by conduction, the foam's purpose is to stop it.
